newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil real ends off 0.14 pct on lower mini-band.
newsitem.headline: Brazil real ends off 0.14 pct on lower mini-band.

text.p: Brazil's real fell 0.14 percent to close at 1.0361 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market after the Central Bank set a weaker mini-band for the currency of 1.0360 to 1.0410 per dollar, dealers said.
The Central Bank set the new trading level for the fluctuation of the real by buying dollars at 1.0360 and selling at 1.0410 reais in a morning auction.
The previous mini-band, set on Dec 5, was between 1.0345 and 1.0395 reais to the dollar.
Although the market was expecting a drop in the mini-band, the 0.15 percent drop was a surprise, dealers said. But banks reacted with calmness, they added.
Dealers said the market still believes the Central Bank is just concentrating mini-band reductions in the beginning of the month aiming to make forex rates more attractive to exports.
Exports are traditionally lower than usual in the second half of December, dealers added.
They also believe that the Central Bank will not change the percentage it intends to drop the mini-band during the month.
So far this month, the mini-band has been lowered 0.35 percent. In the last few months, the mini-band was dropped between 0.5 and 0.6 percent.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real fell 0.13 percent to end at 1.0417 to the dollar, following the drop in the mini-band.
In the illegal parallel market, the real closed at 1.108 per greenback, down 0.73 percent, traders said.
